children: said on Friday it would become the latest blue-chip client to dump KPMG as its auditor following the firm's whistleblower and audit leak scandal.
KPMG has been the Melbourne-based bank's auditor since 1969, making it one of Australia's most long-standing corporate relationships.
ANZ said in a statement it would run a tender process to replace KPMG and finalise that process by April next year. The new auditor would begin in the 2029 financial year, ANZ said.
ANZ did not mention KPMG's scandal in the statement. KPMG did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
KPMG is at the centre of a regulatory and political investigation after a whistleblower alleged the firm shared confidential client information to support bids for auditing work.
The bank said KPMG's key partners working on the ANZ accounts had been rotated, in line with auditing best practices.
"A tenure of this length is no longer considered appropriate and has been under consideration by the board for some time," ANZ said.
ANZ joins a growing number of Australian companies reviewing long-standing audit arrangements with KPMG. Insurance Australia Group
The leaks scandal has shaken up KPMG's executive ranks in Australia, with its chief executive and several senior partners leaving the firm.
The lender said the timing of the tender process was appropriate given the significant transformation program underway and the planned integration of Suncorp Bank.
